options: Every query executed in the account, including its text, user, role, status, and timing
Only queries that failed
Only DDL statements like CREATE and DROP
The current role hierarchy, not query activity
questions.explain: QUERY_HISTORY is a flat log of every statement that ran, regardless of type or outcome, with timing and status.

questions.q: What makes ACCESS_HISTORY a different, narrower view than QUERY_HISTORY?
options: It records the actual tables and columns a query read or wrote, resolved through views and UDFs
It only logs queries run by the ACCOUNTADMIN role
It replaces QUERY_HISTORY entirely on Enterprise Edition
It only shows queries that modified data, never reads
questions.explain: ACCESS_HISTORY goes beyond 'what ran' to 'what data did it actually touch,' including objects accessed indirectly through a view or UDF.

questions.q: Why can't you substitute a text search on query_text for an ACCESS_HISTORY audit?
options: A query selecting from a view never names the underlying base table in its own text, but ACCESS_HISTORY resolves that indirection
query_text is encrypted and cannot be searched
Text search only works on QUERY_METERING_HISTORY
ILIKE is not a valid Snowflake SQL operator
questions.explain: Indirection through views or UDFs means the sensitive table's name may never appear in the query text at all — ACCESS_HISTORY's base_objects_accessed resolves it regardless.

questions.q: What edition requirement and latency apply to ACCESS_HISTORY?
options: Enterprise Edition or higher, with latency of up to 180 minutes (3 hours)
Available on all editions including Standard, with no latency
Business Critical Edition only, with 24-hour latency
Standard Edition only, deprecated on Enterprise Edition
questions.explain: ACCESS_HISTORY requires Enterprise Edition or higher and can lag up to three hours behind real time — not suitable for same-minute incident response.

questions.q: What is the difference between ACCESS_HISTORY's direct_objects_accessed and base_objects_accessed columns?
options: direct_objects_accessed lists objects named directly in the query; base_objects_accessed resolves underlying objects reached through views or UDFs
direct_objects_accessed only applies to INSERT statements
base_objects_accessed is deprecated in favor of direct_objects_accessed
They always contain identical values
questions.explain: direct_objects_accessed reflects what the query literally names; base_objects_accessed traces through any view or UDF indirection to the real underlying objects.
